sentences.text: I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent and perused the materials placed before this Court.
3.The grievance of the petitioner in the writ petition is that the petitioner has already been deprived of his valuable land and possession has also been taken over by the Highways authorities.
The respondent has passed only an interim award way back on 30.06.2016 awarding very meagre compensation, which was received by the petitioner subject to objection.

4.The only grievance of the petitioner is that unless the final award is passed and the matter is referred to the competent civil Court to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis enable the petitioner to seek enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is left high and dry and also not able to realise the fruits of the award of land acquisition compensation.
The petitioner has made a request as early as in November, 2021 and had also sought for furnishing documents under Right to Information Act.
The petitioner has also made a further representation on 20.12.2024 seeking reference to the Court for an enhancement of compensation.

5.In view of the above, this writ petition disposed of in the following manner:
1. The respondent shalla pass final award pursuant to the interim award in Na.Ka.
D1/14323/2011 dated 30.06.2016 within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order;
2.

If the petitioner is aggrieved by the award of compensation in the final award to be published by the respondent, then he shall give objections in writing, if any, within a period of 2 weeks thereafter and the respondent shall refer the matter to the c o m p e t e n t c i v i l C o u r t u n d e r S e c t i o n 2 0 o f t h e T a m i l https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Nadu Highways Act, 2001 to enable the petitioner to seek enhancement of compensation.
3. No costs.
